profile.summary: The MPRabc paper's evaluation of enhancer-gene link predictors on K562 cells. Predicted links are scored against a gold-standard set of 10 356 CRISPRi perturbations (471 positive, 9885 negative) using the benchmarking pipeline of Gschwind et al., with area under the precision-recall curve as the main metric. It is useful to regulatory genomics researchers comparing enhancer-gene models, but it is one paper's run on one cell line.

summary_quotes.text: We report performance on a dataset containing 10 356 CRISPRi perturbations (471 positive, 9885 negative)
The pipeline assesses predictions by intersecting model scores with these labeled pairs and computing the area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC).

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a model can tell which candidate enhancers regulate which genes in K562 cells. The truth set is enhancer-gene pairs tested by CRISPR interference: a pair is positive when perturbing the enhancer significantly reduced the gene's expression. The paper uses the systematic benchmarking pipeline of Gschwind et al., which pools CRISPR perturbation results into a gold standard and asks how well model scores recover them.

quotes.text: The systematic benchmarking pipeline aggregates evidence from clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based perturbations into a gold-standard set of E–G interactions and evaluates model predictions by quantifying their ability to recover these experimentally validated links

Positive examples were E–G pairings validated by CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) perturbations that significantly reduced the target gene’s expression; all other candidate pairings lacking this evidence were treated as negatives

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: Candidate enhancers are DNase-seq peaks called with MACS2, resized to 500 bp, keeping the top 150 000 by read count; every candidate within 5 000 000 bp of a gene's TSS forms a candidate pair. DNase-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq and Hi-C come from ENCODE. Models are evaluated on predefined CRISPRi datasets from Gschwind et al., and the paper reports the K562 set of 10 356 perturbations. MPRabc itself was trained on K562 CRISPRi-labelled pairs, as Gschwind et al. recommend.

quotes.text: Peaks were resized to 500 bp, and the top 150 000 peaks ranked by total read count were retained for downstream analyses.
We considered all candidate CREs within a 5 000 000-bp window of each gene’s transcription start site (TSS) as potential E–G interactions.

DNase-seq, chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by sequencing (ChIP-seq) for histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac), and high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) datasets were obtained from the ENCODE project
does not perform cross-validation. Instead, models are evaluated on predefined CRISPRi datasets provided by Gschwind
We trained and benchmarked our model using the K562 cell line, as recommended by Gschwind

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Model scores are intersected with the labelled pairs and AUPRC is computed; precision at 70% recall is the secondary metric, using the pipeline's default operating point. Uncertainty comes from 10 000 bootstrap replicates of the labelled pairs, with 95% percentile intervals. The paper reports MPRabc at AUPRC 0.707 (95% CI 0.663 to 0.746), against the ABC model at 0.612 and ENCODE-rE2G at 0.634, and ablations that drop the MPRALegNet or Sei features.

quotes.text: The pipeline assesses predictions by intersecting model scores with these labeled pairs and computing the area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC).
We adhered to the pipeline’s default settings, using the threshold corresponding to 70% recall for binary predictions.
Specifically, the pipeline generated 10 000 bootstrap replicates of labeled E–G pairs and recomputed AUPRC for each replicate.
We report 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using the percentile method
MPRabc achieved an AUPRC of 0.707 (95% CI: 0.663–0.746), the highest performance among E–G predictors with comparable inputs
MPRabc outperformed the ABC model (AUPRC = 0.612; 95% CI: 0.567–0.656) and ENCODE-rE2G (AUPRC = 0.634; 95% CI: 0.587–0.684).

notes: The record groups the paper's K562 evaluation; the underlying gold standard and pipeline belong to Gschwind et al. (ENCODE-rE2G), which may deserve its own benchmark record. The Zenodo record 17822027 holds the paper's analysis datasets (Data.zip); it is not shown to contain the CRISPRi gold standard. A second deposit, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20162603, is named in the paper and was not fetched.
